question: In the context of the passage, which idiom best conveys the meaning of "reconciles the persistent dichotomy between learning and livelihood" as used in the final paragraph?

options.text: Hit the nail on the head

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Bridge the gap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"bridge the gap"** means:

 
 
• To connect two things or to reconcile differences between them. (अंतर को पाटना)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The new policies aim to bridge the gap between rich and poor.
 
• **"Correct answer"** means:
 
 
• Referring to the specific answer that properly defines or fits the context of the question. (सही उत्तर)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The correct answer to the quiz question assured him a perfect score.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: **Bridge the gap**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Hit the nail on the head** (बिलकुल सही बात कहना): To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.

 
 
• **Example:** She really hit the nail on the head with her comments about the company's inefficiencies.
 
 
 
• **Burn the midnight oil** (रात देर तक काम करना): To work late into the night.
 
 
• **Example:** He burned the midnight oil to finish the project on time.
 
 
 
• **Throw in the towel** (हार मान लेना): To give up or admit defeat.
 
 
• **Example:** After months of struggling, he finally threw in the towel and closed his business.
